note: Results appear here on election night. Polls close 7 PM Central in Massachusetts and Houston, 9 PM Central in most of Idaho (10 PM in the panhandle).

measures.name: Question 8
measures.title: End recreational marijuana sales
measures.yes: Bans licensed retail sales of recreational marijuana starting January 1, 2028. The medical program stays, and existing stores could try to convert to medical.
measures.no: Keeps the legal recreational market Massachusetts voters approved in 2016.
measures.context: No state has ever shut down a legal recreational market. Polls: UNH 71% no / 24% yes; MassINC 61% no / 27% yes / 11% undecided. Governor Maura Healey and Senators Warren and Markey oppose it. The repeal side has out-raised the no side about 2 to 1.

measures.name: HJR 4
measures.title: Only the legislature can legalize marijuana
measures.yes: Amends the Idaho constitution so only the legislature can legalize marijuana or other psychoactive drugs. Citizens permanently lose the ability to do it by ballot initiative.
measures.no: Keeps the citizen initiative process as it is.
measures.context: Idaho is one of the last states where marijuana is completely illegal. Lawmakers passed HJR 4 58–10 in the House and 29–6 in the Senate, and a medical marijuana initiative fell short of the 2026 ballot.
measures.closes: 9:00 PM Central (10 PM in the panhandle)

measures.name: Proposition A
measures.title: Marijuana arrests become the lowest police priority
measures.yes: Writes into the city charter that low-level marijuana arrests are the Houston Police Department's lowest priority. It does NOT legalize marijuana; possession is still a crime under Texas law.
measures.no: Leaves police enforcement priorities as they are.
measures.context: Ground Game Texas gathered about 40,000 signatures. The Houston police officers' union opposes it. A 2025 Texas appeals court ruling against similar local measures means even a yes vote could face a legal fight. Early voting starts October 19.
